configurePresets.name: cpu-dev
configurePresets.description: CPU-only debug build: SQL/planner/optimizer/storage/Parquet metadata path without CUDA/libcudf.

configurePresets.name: gpu-dev
configurePresets.description: Enables CUDA + libcudf + RMM. Requires the CUDA toolkit and a RAPIDS libcudf/RMM install.

configurePresets.name: gpu-release
configurePresets.description: Enables CUDA + libcudf + RMM, optimized (RelWithDebInfo, matching the CPU-only `cpu-release` preset). Requires the CUDA toolkit and a RAPIDS libcudf/RMM install, same as `gpu-dev`.

configurePresets.name: server-dev
configurePresets.description: CPU-only debug build with the Arrow Flight SQL server (kernellake-server) enabled. Requires libarrow-flight-dev, libarrow-flight-sql-dev, and gRPC.

configurePresets.name: otel-dev
configurePresets.description: CPU-only debug build with OpenTelemetry OTLP/gRPC tracing+metrics+logs export enabled. Requires opentelemetry-cpp-dev. Combine directly with -DKERNELLAKE_BUILD_SERVER=ON (no dedicated combined preset yet) to also exercise the Flight SQL server's query span.

configurePresets.name: cpu-coverage
configurePresets.description: cpu-dev plus gcc's --coverage instrumentation (-fprofile-arcs -ftest-coverage at compile time, --coverage at link time), for CI's coverage job -- see .github/workflows/ci.yml's `coverage` job and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's CI section. Not for day-to-day development: every translation unit rebuilds slower and larger under instrumentation, and .gcda files accumulate on every test run (`ctest --preset cpu-coverage` again overwrites them, not merges) so stale ones must be cleared with a fresh build directory rather than reused across unrelated runs.

configurePresets.name: gpu-coverage
configurePresets.description: gpu-dev plus gcc's --coverage instrumentation, same rationale as cpu-coverage -- for CI's gpu-coverage job (self-hosted GPU runner only, see .github/workflows/ci.yml). This project has no .cu files of its own (src/execution_gpu/*.cpp are plain C++ calling into cudf/rmm's precompiled libraries), so gcov works here exactly as it does under cpu-coverage; only KERNELLAKE_WITH_CUDA=ON's own translation units need a real CUDA toolkit + GPU to build/run at all. gpu-dev's CMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER hardcodes /usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc (the Docker image's layout); a self-hosted runner whose nvcc lives elsewhere (e.g. an apt-installed toolkit) should override it explicitly at configure time (`-DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER=$(command -v nvcc)`) rather than this preset guessing a path that wouldn't generalize.
